questions.question: What is the current conservation status and wild-population trend of African elephant?
questions.previous_ai_answer: **Not established from this inventory row.** No taxon-matched current IUCN assessment year, population definition and trend are recorded for this entry. A current assessment must be checked before assigning a category or numeric wild population estimate.
questions.verdict: The historic Dubbo animals were **African savanna elephants (*Loxodonta africana*)**. The [amended IUCN 2022 assessment](https://doi.org/10.2305/IUCN.UK.2022-2.RLTS.T181008073A223031019.en), assessed 13 November 2020, classifies them as **Endangered (EN), global trend decreasing**, with roughly **60% long-term decline** in the assessment. The separate **African forest elephant (*L. cyclotis*)** is **Critically Endangered, declining** ([IUCN 2021](https://doi.org/10.2305/IUCN.UK.2021-1.RLTS.T181007989A181019888.en)). Neither species' assessment provides an unambiguous current single-species wild headcount; the 2016 ~415,000 estimate combines the two, and the [2025 improved forest estimates](https://iucn.org/press-release/202511/dna-methods-help-uncover-further-african-forest-elephants-species-remains) should not be interpreted as proven population growth.
